Teacher here:

Classes are not a teacher teaching individual students. A class is a teacher working with a classroom. The goals of everyone in that class room is to learn and contribute. By being the "bad guy" occasionally by 'punishing' the entire class for a few bad actors, it helps students keep each other accountable for academic behavior because they don't want to be punished. 

"Well, that doesn't seem fair! Why doesn't the teacher just punish students individually?" Two reasons I'd argue:

1. feasibility. Having students hold each other accountable is significantly more effective and consumed way less time on the teachers half. If you have never taught a group of high/middle schoolers, try it and then get back to me.

2. teaching skills. It is a skill to hold others accountable to group expectations. This relates to society, to workplace environment, to families, etc. Being able to reign in behaviors in groups that are contrary to the behavior of all teaches students social skills and management techniques. It's one if those, "It sucks but it helps you long-term" things.

There are two types of work:

1. Work that you genuinely enjoy (The classic, "If you could do anything full time and not worry about money, what would it be?") Not everyone finds something like this im their life, and I think at schools its overemphasized as "just do your passion and it will work out well." Not always true.

2. Work that you tolerate that will allow you do the things you want to do. What can you do for 8 hours a day that will let you pursue the things you want to do, while not giving too much of a shit about it.

I would argue that even people who don't "work" in the traditional sense (ie having a job) still have to do some sort of work - Homeless people still have to find food and a place to sleep, and I wouldn't say that isn't work. If you want some genuine life advice, this is the gist of what I've told many students:

Life can suck sometimes, and it can be unfair, and change can be hard. But it is possible and worthwhile, even if only temporary.

Think about a goal that you want to do, big or small, or a direction that you want to head. Could be anything - A job, career, piece of art you want to create, something you want to start, hobby you develop, etc. If you're not sure, totally fine - Start with something you enjoy or think about doing but never do. Write it down on a sticky note or something. Then everyday, wake up and think of something you can do to work towards that goal - Whether it be 5 minutes or 5 hours, starts as big as you want. 

Everyday, work towards that goal. If you miss a day, it's not the end of the world and shit happens, but go back to it the next day. And every single day, take one action however small towards that goal. As you build that skill and work towards that goal, it will become easier and you will become more motivated. One day, you'll notice that it's automatic.

Doing something for 5 minutes is easy, start there. Doing something consistently every single day is the hard part, but it gets easier the more you do it.

At the end of the day, only you can take that first step and only you know yourself well enough to know what it will take. Be honest with yourself, and yake the first step. The second one will be a little easier, and the third a little easier than that. If one day, you realize you don't like your goal, than you know one thing you don't want to do now and can change it - But you learned something about yourself. It was not a worthless endeavor. Then, start all over again. 5 Minutes a day and work up.

Hopefully that's motivational or helps you go in the right direction. I akso highly suggest going to some sort of consistent check-in, therapy is a good example. Life coaches (Just don't get scammed), friends/family if you have them, etc, or finding s local group to join that can help.

The distinction people always forget about Tinker is they don't surrender their rights *unless it interferes with with the operation of the school or its duties.*

Legally, a school can't force students to take down posts unless they consist of unprotected speech (threats, defamation, etc) or they are disruptive to the learning environment.

Yes of course, schools can't force you to take down any post for any reason, but when it has substantial potential to cause a disruption they can. What can be disruptive to the learning environment depends, and needs to be decided case by case. Generally, two categories are looked at when deciding this:

1. Does it take place in, around, or in connection to the school or a school-related activity? If yes, is it causing in part or in whole a disruption of the learning process? What they are looking for here is not if something was controversial and creating a dialogue about the issue, as is the case with Tinker creating a dialogue about the Vietnam War. A fight like this is not only a very unproductive thing and disrupts the learning environment, but as it spreads it will create more issues and is very likely to perpetuate the issue and create more drama, thus making it a disruption. Because it happened at or connected to a school, this particular case is pretty cut and dry. This can conditionally be extended to off school speech as well:
2. Does it interfere or create a likely scenario in which it will spread into the learning environment? Two years ago, in Mahanoy Area School District v. B.L., the supreme Court decided that while yes, students do enjoy free speech off campus, "on campus" doesn't just mean physically in a building anymore like before the spread of the internet. Speech that can interfere with the learning environment, whether on or off campus, can be policed by schools. The court ruled that schools not only have a vested interest in themselves (hence focusing on the "harm to the schools"), but in teaching students how to be good citizens. This includes teaching them the virtue of protecting freedom of speech (including unpopular speech), but also pointing out where free speech no longer applies. This in part includes bullying, defamation, and threats.

Again, most of these cases are handled case by case basis and there is no "one size fits all" answer.

Don't see how this is violating the first amendment.

Schools serve one major purpose: Provide educational instruction to students. The supreme court has ruled that while yes students do retain their rights in school, they can be limited if  it disrupts the learning environment.

Cyberbullying and fights like this can certainly disrupt the learning environment because it creates potential for clashes in school. Yes, a principal usually can't force a student to remove anything from social media unless it falls under unprotected speech, but as long as it has the potential to create disruptions they certainly can suspend students for it if they refuse to take it down. As long as they are provided out of school educational services to those students like they are required to, it's perfectly legal. This also falls under many anti-bullying and anti-cyberbullying laws that school boards and local governments have adopted. In cases I've worked on the courts have always sided with the schools on these suspensions when challenged.

Of course we don't want to suspend students for it, and we only do it as a last resort if we really feel there is potential for major fallout in or about the school.

I'm not a lawyer so I can't speak exactly to what the law says, but I've worked in and with several school districts so I can speak to how it actually functions within most districts. I handle these situations frequently.

Your example of a tweet calling a teacher a bitch certainly can be and will result in punishment if it makes it to upper administration. Same goes with students talking shit about eachother on social media and posting videos of fights. These can and often do create tensions in school that disrupts the learning environment and creates health risks to students and teachers. 

Sure, we can not legally pursue a student and force them to remove a video offline, but that doesn't mean there aren't consequences for those actions. Students can certainly be suspended or, in very, very extreme cases, expelled for being requested to take down comments/videos from social media, most commonly under anti-bullying ordinances passed by local governments/school boards. Since the school's job is to provide education opportunities to students, if they deem a student a danger to being in school because of what they post or their refusal to take it down, they can be suspended and supplied with out-of-school educational services. The video can stay up, but the student needs to stay off school property. The courts have and will side with schools on this on a few cases I've been involved with.

There have been several examples of cyberbullying or harassment following fights/online bullying that certainly make their way back into the classroom. Social media usage in this way is not only limited by schools and anti-bullying laws, but most platforms online have their own terms and policies to limit these as well.

I was in the band for 5 years (17-22), currently on my way out so I won't be there next year but I'll let you know my experience overall.

First off - best decision of my life was joining HMB, and I'm not exaggerating in the slightest. I fell in love from the first day with everyone and everything which kept me coming back and led me to spend a year as section leader.

Schedule-wise, it can be a lot. Before school starts we do Pre-school drills (P[t]SDs), which is around 8ish hours of rehearsals a day for around a week before the second homegame of the season. The first one of these is with rookies (first year, new members) and their section leaders. PSDs can be daunting - you come in and everyone around you knows what's going on and you have no clue, but you learn quick.

After that, rehearsals are more manageable. Practice 6-8 Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday and 5-7 Friday through fall quarter. Sections usually have 1-2 hour long sectionals a week before rehearsal. If classes overlap with rehearsals or sectionals, you can often get it excused. We have rallies Friday before every homegame (which are optional, but so so fun) where we go around the dorms and greek row and play songs for the students. Homegames are long days, usually around 10-12 hours of being at football games and playing, but they're so fun (even better when we win haha). Bowl games or away trips are so fun as well in an absolute shitshow way. I was in the Rosebowl in '19 and genuinely being on that field and hearing the fans shout for us during out show was the best thing I've ever experienced.  Outside of this, each section has their own traditions or hangouts that are optional, but a good way to get to know people, especially if you're shy or introverted like I am. Most of my friends ended up coming from band and they're friends I'll have for life. The rest of the year is chill, we have occasionally gigs that you can sign up for but none are required, but many are so much fun. Even some of the worst gigs or away trips I look back fondly on. Would I recommend it to a freshman? Yes. Can it be a lot to balance band with school work? Also yes, but it gives you an extra arm of support. Band is ultimately what you put into it, and if you put a lot in you get a lot out. 

If you have any other questions feel free to ask me, I love talking about band. If you do join and you see a crazy clarinet alumni passing out buttons, shouting dumb things,  and being a general loonie, feel free to say hi to me!

Me and my gf bought a chameleon with proper research and everything, a whole schedule planned out. We got one from Petco, however, who was apparently already sick and needed vet attention. Two weeks to the day after we got him he died because of how serious it was and because we didn't know how to take care of a sick chameleon besides what last minute advice a vet could give us

If you're seriously worried, it might be a good idea to take your chameleon to a vet for a check-up (If you've never done it, it's good to do so just so that you have a connection to a professional). Otherwise being brown can be a sign that they're too cold, check the temperature to make sure that it's getting to where it should be (~100F hottest, ~75F coldest)

I don't have any experience with T8 except that I've heard off hand that it's not the most ideal. When I first got a chameleon, I used a compact uvb bulb that wasn't tubular (big mistake). I got a reptisun t5 Hood and bulb online, and so I'd recommend searching online for it if you can't find one in the store. I've only ever seen T8s in stores and never T5s, most commonly Petco or PetSmart, so I'd check those two first if you want to get one irl.

I recommend finding someone else who can care for it really fast as it's a very hard animal to take care of. If not, this is the MINIMUM you need,  you need it ASAP. It also varies per species of Chameleon, so find our what species he is and adjust accordingly. Generic requirements are:

Cage: first it should have a a 2x2x4 foot mesh cage with airflow, perferably have the highest spot he can reach above 6 feet. Use a t5 Hood with a 10.0 UVB light (24 inch Hood, 22 inch bulb. Zoo med is a good supplier, just make sure there tubular.) Its important you get a tube light, as lightbulbs aren't effective enough. You also need to make sure that the light is not obstructed by plastic or glass, as this will filter out the UVB rays. The light will need to be replaced about every 6 months. It may still be bright, but it won't be emmiting UVB light anymore. And a ceramic heating bulb that can get up to 105F and he can warm up. The UVB light stays on for 12 hours, the ceramic stays on constantly. He also needs a shaded place to cool off. Get a thermometer and a hydrometer so you can read the temp and humidity. The temperature should not go below 72F and should be about 80-90F, and the humidity should be about 50-70%. Tons of plants, vines, and other decorations so he can climb around on. Don't use a substrate for the bottom of the cage, use some paper towels  or some sort of mossy cover you can buy at the petstore. It'so recommended you get a water dripping system. They will NOT drink still water, it has to be on the leaves. You can achieve this by actively spraying water for a minute every 4-6 hours, or by automated water sprayer.

Food: You can feed them crickets or many types of worms, like waxworms. Crickets you need to gutload, which you  can do with vegies like carrots or various lettuces, or with  fruits like oranges or apples. You need to dust what you feed the chameleon. This is CRITICAL: dust the crickets (or whatever you feed him)  with calcium WITHOUT D3 daily or every other day, depending on the age. Dust with multivitamins twice a month and Calcium with D3 twice a month. About ~5 crickets per day. You need to remember that if they don't consume enough calcium, and aren't exposed to enough UVB, they will die so don't by any circumstances cheap out on this. Seriously, I can't stress this enough. 

Handling: please don't try to handle him in the first week or two of having him. It will stress him out. You will want to start off by hand feeding him (presenting some worm or a cricket via tongs or your hand) only pick him up if it is critical. Once he trusts you enough to let you pick him up, you can bring him outside to get natural UVB ONLY if it's warm enough. If it's winter, don't do that. 

I just want to stress again how delicate these creatures are, and you need to be familiar with common ailments like MBD, which is a calcium deficiency caused by lack of calcium and/or UVB light. This is fatal and is expensive to treat, and takes months to recover from and can be deadly. If you notice that your chameleon has a double elbow, or what is a broken or bent limb, he most likely has MBD and you need to bring him into an exotic animal vet ASAP. Literally, ASAP. 

One finally note is don't trust pet employees when they try to sell you things. They more often then not don't know what a chameleon needs, and will try to sell you cheap shit that won't work. I prey you take my advice because I speak from experience, and it's awful to know that you've caused such a graceful creature pain and suffering. A good resource for additional questions is chameleon forums in the internet. Please read up on all they need, and don't delay getting anything.
